article_content: In a significant judicial decision, three former Atlanta police officers were condemned with prison sentences ranging from six to ten years for their involvement in a botched drug raid that tragically resulted in the death of a nonagenarian, Kathryn Johnston. Jason Smith, Greg Junnier, and Arthur Tesler, previously affected by an incorrect light sentence due to an administrative oversight, have had their sentences rectified. Smith's sentence was corrected to ten years while Junnier and Tesler's sentences were set at six and five years, respectively. The context of this miscarriage of justice came to light following an investigation that brought to the fore intensely negligent practices by the ex-officers, as they erroneously permitted a vendetta against an inflamed civil rights backdrop. The case profoundly affected the Atlanta Police Department, forcing a mandatory reorganization of the drug unit and a rigorous introspection about the administration's previously held habits.
translated_content: Hoy, se emitió un fallo significativo en Atlanta, Georgia. La participación irregular de Jason Smith, Greg Junnier y Arthur Tesler, exacerbada por sentencias anteriormente equivocadas, ha sido atendida. Smith debe cumplir diez años en prisión, mientras que Junnier y Tesler deben cumplir seis y cinco años, respectivamente. Este quebranto de las dignidades civiles, surgido de negligencias policiales maliciosas, ha provocado una necesaria reestructuración del Colegio de Detectives de Narcóticos de Atlanta.
